**Accepted values:** `parseEncoding` recognizes exactly `auto`, `none`, `utf-8`, `utf-16`, `utf-16le`, `utf-16be`, and `latin1` (src/scan.zig:107-114). Anything else returns `null` (src/scan.zig:115), and the callers then fall back to `.auto` (src/main.zig:2285, 2433, 2608).

**`--encoding=utf-16` without a BOM:** A doc comment in src/scan.zig:99 says `utf-16` means "BOM decides, else LE (rg does the same)". So with no BOM, the file is treated as little-endian UTF-16.

**Caveats:** The context shows only part of that doc comment, and it doesn't include the decoding code. I can't confirm how the BOM check is implemented. I also can't tell from this output whether the CLI reports an error on an unrecognized value or silently uses `auto`, since the arg-parsing validation isn't shown. The fallback to `.auto` in main.zig is all I can see.
